title: The Ceiling, and the Sharing Puzzle

scenes.tts: If N G F keeps neurons alive, can extra N G F make a ganglion bigger without limit?
scenes.caption: If NGF keeps neurons alive, can extra NGF make a ganglion bigger without limit?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Ceiling, and the Sharing Puzzle. A ganglion with an arrow pointing up and a question mark.
scenes.narration: If NGF keeps neurons alive, can extra NGF make a ganglion bigger without limit?

scenes.tts: Give a chick embryo extra N G F every day, through the period when its neurons normally die.
scenes.caption: Give a chick embryo extra NGF every day, through the period when its neurons normally die.
scenes.visual: A chick embryo schematic with a daily NGF drop across a death-period band on a timeline.
scenes.narration: Give a chick embryo extra NGF every day, through the period when its neurons normally die.

scenes.tts: Predict. No change? More survivors? New ganglia in the wrong places? Fibres invading every tissue?
scenes.visual: Four option cards: no change; more survive; new ganglia in wrong places; fibres invade every tissue.
scenes.narration: Predict. No change? More survivors? New ganglia in the wrong places? Fibres invading every tissue?

scenes.tts: More of the neurons survive than normal.
scenes.visual: The more survive card lights up. In the ganglion, fewer neurons fade than in the control.
scenes.narration: More of the neurons survive than normal.

scenes.tts: Survivors also grow larger and sprout more fibres. But no neuron changes its type.
scenes.visual: Survivors swell and branch. The type-change card is struck through.
scenes.narration: Survivors also grow larger and sprout more fibres. But no neuron changes its type.

scenes.tts: In nineteen eighty-one, Hamburger, Brunso-Bechtold and Yip counted chick dorsal root ganglia across the death period.
scenes.caption: In 1981, Hamburger, Brunso-Bechtold and Yip counted chick dorsal root ganglia across the death period.
scenes.visual: Credit: Hamburger, Brunso-Bechtold and Yip, 1981. Counts at several stages in chick dorsal root ganglia.
scenes.narration: In 1981, Hamburger, Brunso-Bechtold and Yip counted chick dorsal root ganglia across the death period.

scenes.tts: N G F reduced the normal death.
scenes.caption: NGF reduced the normal death.
scenes.visual: A label on the counts: NGF reduced the normal death.
scenes.narration: NGF reduced the normal death.

scenes.tts: How do you know they were saved, not born? Count neurons and dying nuclei at several stages.
scenes.visual: Checklist card, item 1: count neurons and dying nuclei across the window.
scenes.narration: How do you know they were saved, not born? Count neurons and dying nuclei at several stages.

scenes.tts: Mark dividing cells. Then check that the neurons carry markers of their usual type.
scenes.visual: Items 2 and 3: mark division; check identity, such as tyrosine hydroxylase in sympathetic neurons.
scenes.narration: Mark dividing cells. Then check that the neurons carry markers of their usual type.

scenes.tts: Very early in the chick, extra N G F can also increase division in the primary sympathetic ganglia.
scenes.caption: Very early in the chick, extra NGF can also increase division in the primary sympathetic ganglia.
scenes.visual: A primary sympathetic ganglion in an early chick embryo with dividing cells marked. Label: early chick embryo.
scenes.narration: Very early in the chick, extra NGF can also increase division in the primary sympathetic ganglia.

scenes.tts: That happens before sympathetic axons reach their targets. The extra division is N G F acting as something other than a survival factor.
scenes.caption: That happens before sympathetic axons reach their targets. The extra division is NGF acting as something other than a survival factor.
scenes.visual: Axons not yet at their targets. Labels: more division, not a survival effect; a little less death. Division and death counts separate the two.
scenes.narration: That happens before sympathetic axons reach their targets. The extra division is NGF acting as something other than a survival factor.

scenes.tts: Now the limit. A survival factor cannot save a neuron that was never made.
scenes.visual: A row of neurons that exist, and an empty outline labelled never made, which no factor can fill.
scenes.narration: Now the limit. A survival factor cannot save a neuron that was never made.

scenes.tts: Take a ganglion that has made a thousand neurons, with none added. Each needs one unit a day from a shared supply.
scenes.caption: Take a ganglion that has made 1,000 neurons, with none added. Each needs one unit a day from a shared supply.
scenes.visual: Ideal allocation model card: fixed cohort, no new neurons or immigration. N = 1,000 neurons already made; each needs q = 1 unit per day; shared supply F = 500, 1,000 or 3,000 units per day. Label: illustrative.
scenes.narration: Take a ganglion that has made 1,000 neurons, with none added. Each needs one unit a day from a shared supply.

scenes.tts: With five hundred units a day, the target limits survivors. With three thousand, the number made limits them.
scenes.caption: With 500 units a day, the target limits survivors. With 3,000, the number made limits them.
scenes.visual: A three-row table on screen: 500 units per day, at most 500 survive, target limits; 1,000 units per day, at most 1,000, both; 3,000 units per day, at most 1,000, number made limits. Label: ideal allocation model.
scenes.narration: With 500 units a day, the target limits survivors. With 3,000, the number made limits them.

scenes.tts: In this ideal model, survivors are at most the smaller of the neurons made and how many the supply can support. It is a budget bound, not a dose law.
scenes.visual: The rule on screen: S ≤ min(N, floor(F/q)). Labels: ideal allocation model; fixed cohort; a support-budget bound, not a law relating an injected NGF dose to neuron number.
scenes.narration: In this ideal model, survivors are at most the smaller of the neurons made and how many the supply can support. It is a budget bound, not a dose law.

scenes.tts: Extra factor raises the second term. Acting as a survival factor, nothing raises the first.
scenes.visual: The survival ceiling plot: an ideal upper bound that rises with supply, then flattens at the line neurons made. A dashed real curve sits below it. Labels: ideal upper bound; real survival can fall short.
scenes.narration: Extra factor raises the second term. Acting as a survival factor, nothing raises the first.

scenes.tts: Now a puzzle. Spread those five hundred units evenly over all thousand neurons.
scenes.caption: Now a puzzle. Spread those 500 units evenly over all 1,000 neurons.
scenes.visual: 500 units per day spread evenly across 1,000 neurons: every neuron glows at half brightness.
scenes.narration: Now a puzzle. Spread those 500 units evenly over all 1,000 neurons.

scenes.tts: Predict. Every neuron gets half of what it needs. How many survive?
scenes.visual: Question card: every neuron at half; how many survive?
scenes.narration: Predict. Every neuron gets half of what it needs. How many survive?

scenes.tts: It depends. Every neuron is equally short, so all are at risk at once.
scenes.visual: All the neurons dim together.
scenes.narration: It depends. Every neuron is equally short, so all are at risk at once.

scenes.tts: Each death frees factor for the rest. But a neuron already committed to dying cannot use it.
scenes.caption: Each death frees factor for the rest. But a neuron already committed to dying cannot use it.
scenes.visual: One neuron fades and its share of the continuing supply drifts to neighbours; a neuron marked committed lets it pass. Label: assumes the supply can be redirected. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Each death frees factor for the rest. But a neuron already committed to dying cannot use it.

scenes.tts: So the count depends on timing. Slow commitment and quick sharing leave close to five hundred.
scenes.caption: So the count depends on timing. Slow commitment and quick sharing leave close to 500.
scenes.visual: Two dials: how fast neurons commit; how fast freed factor is shared. Slow commit, quick share: about 500 remain. Label: illustrative.
scenes.narration: So the count depends on timing. Slow commitment and quick sharing leave close to 500.

scenes.tts: Fast commitment leaves far fewer, perhaps none. Equal sharing alone does not say how many survive.
scenes.visual: The dials turn: fast commit, slow share; most neurons fade. No count shown. Label: depends on timing.
scenes.narration: Fast commitment leaves far fewer, perhaps none. Equal sharing alone does not say how many survive.

scenes.tts: When supply is short, matching it means the factor ends up with some neurons, not spread over all.
scenes.visual: Some neurons brighten fully while others fade. Label: factor ends up with some neurons.
scenes.narration: When supply is short, matching it means the factor ends up with some neurons, not spread over all.

scenes.tts: Slow, random loss can get there. Competition that picks winners early is another route.
scenes.visual: Two paths to the same bright subset: slow random fading, and a few neurons brightening early. Label: two routes.
scenes.narration: Slow, random loss can get there. Competition that picks winners early is another route.

scenes.tts: In mouse sympathetic neurons, evidence supports a model of active competition.
scenes.visual: Label: mouse sympathetic neurons, a supported model.
scenes.narration: In mouse sympathetic neurons, evidence supports a model of active competition.

scenes.tts: N G F raises its own receptor, track A, in the neurons that receive it. A neuron that gets a little more can take up still more.
scenes.caption: NGF raises its own receptor, TrkA, in the neurons that receive it. A neuron that gets a little more can take up still more.
scenes.visual: One neuron brightens, grows more TrkA receptors, and pulls in more NGF particles.
scenes.narration: NGF raises its own receptor, TrkA, in the neurons that receive it. A neuron that gets a little more can take up still more.

scenes.tts: Strong signallers release two related factors, B D N F and N T four. They act through another receptor, P seventy-five.
scenes.caption: Strong signallers release two related factors, BDNF and NT-4. They act through another receptor, p75.
scenes.visual: Arrows labelled BDNF and NT-4 run from the bright neuron to a dim neighbour bearing a receptor labelled p75.
scenes.narration: Strong signallers release two related factors, BDNF and NT-4. They act through another receptor, p75.

scenes.tts: They push neighbours with weak N G F signalling toward death. Winners are amplified, and losers are punished.
scenes.caption: They push neighbours with weak NGF signalling toward death. Winners are amplified, and losers are punished.
scenes.visual: The dim neighbour fades. Caption: winners amplified, losers punished. Credit: Deppmann and colleagues, 2008.
scenes.narration: They push neighbours with weak NGF signalling toward death. Winners are amplified, and losers are punished.

scenes.tts: One caution. The ceiling holds only for the population measured. Limb motor neurons do not depend on N G F.
scenes.caption: One caution. The ceiling holds only for the population measured. Limb motor neurons do not depend on NGF.
scenes.visual: Caution card: limb motor neurons, not NGF-dependent; several other factors each reduce part of their death in chick.
scenes.narration: One caution. The ceiling holds only for the population measured. Limb motor neurons do not depend on NGF.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: extra N G F saves neurons, but never more than were made. How many survive depends on how the factor is shared.
scenes.caption: Takeaway: extra NGF saves neurons, but never more than were made. How many survive depends on how the factor is shared.
scenes.visual: Closing card: at most the number made; sharing decides how close survivors come.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: extra NGF saves neurons, but never more than were made. How many survive depends on how the factor is shared.
